sections.name: Stingwings
sections.card:
Summary: Fast flying mutant insects, often met in swarms of up to five. They sting with venom and fly erratically.
Weak points: Use V.A.T.S.: its speed and erratic flight make it hard to hit otherwise. It is fragile, so a few shots kill it, even at mid-level.
Looks like: A large mutated insect whose scorpion-like tail ends in a bulb-shaped sting. Glowing stingwings light up from the radiation they absorbed.
Tips: It circles you, dives in for one hit, then circles again. Going near a sap-oozing nest brings out several to defend it.

sections.name: Mole rats
sections.card:
Summary: Fast, territorial pests found from the Red Rocket truck stop to the Glowing Sea. They are weak next to many other enemies, but a swarm can hide and attack from behind.
Weak points: Most weapons kill a standard mole rat in one hit, as it has only 15 hit points. Rabid ones are tougher and their bites hurt over time, but they are still weak.
Looks like: Pink and hairless, with big front teeth and small eyes. Their size runs from a house cat to a large dog, perhaps larger.
Tips: They tunnel to dodge you or sneak up, but a faint tunnel outline shows their path. Landminer mole rats have fragmentation mines on their backs that explode on impact and hurt anything close.

sections.name: Bloodbugs
sections.card:
Summary: Swarming mutated insects that feed on blood through a needle-like proboscis. They can spit the blood back at you for heavy radiation damage.
Weak points: Damage its blood sac to take away its spit, though the sac recovers given time. Its proboscis cannot get through power armor.
Looks like: A muddy-brown insect about two feet long, with six limbs and a long proboscis between its compound eyes. The rare red widow variant is tinted red.
Tips: A brahmin corpse drained of blood and covered in big stings is a strong sign bloodbugs are near. They cling to ceilings and walls, so an empty-looking room may hold a swarm.

sections.name: Radscorpions
sections.card:
Summary: Fast, aggressive mutated scorpions that can burrow, found mostly in the Glowing Sea. A few hits from their claws and tail do heavy damage.
Weak points: Aim for the face, the only weak spot, though it is small. Armor-piercing mods and the Penetrating legendary effect do more damage through their armor.
Looks like: A far larger descendant of the emperor scorpion. Albinos are white, deathskulls reddish, glowing ones green.
Tips: If shot from afar it burrows and surfaces near you, so stand on rocks, metal or wood first. Deathskull radscorpions level with you, so they cannot be pacified.

sections.name: Yao guai
sections.card:
Summary: A vicious mutated black bear. Wild ones go after almost anything they meet, deathclaws included.
Looks like: A big mutated bear. Albinos are paler, rabid ones have red welts, and dusky ones are darker and more scarred.
Tips: Every attack staggers you, even blocked ones, so time your melee swings or it hits you again. Headshots do no bonus damage, and Animal Friend fails on a dusky yao guai, which levels with you.

sections.name: Mirelurks
sections.card:
Summary: Mutated crustaceans of swamps, coasts and sewers, usually in groups. Most have a thick shell that even powerful ballistic weapons struggle to get through.
Weak points: Its face has no armor but is small; a charging mirelurk often covers it until close combat starts. Its limbs are softer than the body, but not as soft as the face.
Looks like: Most adults have a shell and pincers like a horseshoe crab, while the hunter looks like a lobster. A buried one shows only its rounded shell back, like a large smooth rock.
Tips: Cripple both sets of legs on a standard mirelurk and it cannot move or attack, even up close. Mines and attacks from below are things it cannot defend against.

sections.name: Raiders
sections.card:
Summary: Hostile gangs all over the Commonwealth, especially around Boston. They guard their turf fiercely against anyone outside the gang.
Weak points: A common raider has little health and falls to a few hits from basic weapons.
Looks like: Raider scum usually wear crude welded or leather armor. Wasters and veterans can have combat armor, and scavvers are the raiders most often seen in power armor.
Tips: Psychos use chems, charge into melee and may throw grenades. Raiders will not chase you into Boston Common; they call it deadly and retreat.

sections.name: Sentry bots
sections.card:
Summary: A rare combat robot of the heaviest class, usually carrying a missile launcher and a minigun. It is fast, agile and tough enough to survive a direct mini nuke.
Weak points: Aim for the two fusion cores it exposes when it vents steam during a long fight. With the Penetrator perk you can target them in V.A.T.S. at once.
Looks like: A bulky robot about as tall as a human in power armor and almost twice as wide. Gunner sentry bots are tinted a faded green.
Tips: Its death blast matches a mini nuke, and it often charges you if you get too close. Disarm both main weapons and it rushes you to self-destruct; it drops at least two fusion cores.

sections.name: Assaultrons
sections.card:
Summary: A fast, aggressive robot that usually rushes you in melee, and most models carry a head-mounted laser.
Weak points: Shoot its head while the laser charges and its plates peel back; a crippled head loses the laser. Destroy a limb without killing it and it explodes like a mini nuke; killing it first avoids that.
Looks like: A claw-handed robot. Red energy gathers around its head as the laser charges.
Tips: Take cover while the laser charges for 6-7 seconds; it then stands still and fires for 2-3 seconds. The blast can badly hurt even a high-level character who has no cover.

sections.name: Mister Gutsy
sections.card:
Summary: A combat version of the civilian Mister Handy, armed with a 10mm submachine gun, laser or flamer. The submachine gun shreds low-level characters in seconds, even in power armor.
Weak points: Shoot out an eye to spoil its aim, or the thruster to slow it and stop its strafing. Destroying every arm sends it on a suicide rush at you.
Looks like: Its back carries the words "Mister Handy".
Tips: Looking at a neutral Mister Gutsy turns it hostile if your power armor has a targeting HUD mod. A Colonel Gutsy can appear from level 46 up and levels with you.

sections.name: Fat Man
sections.card:
Summary: A shoulder-mounted launcher, formally the M42 nuclear catapult, that lobs mini nukes in an arc.
Uses: Angle it upward for anything past about 20 yards, where a level shot lands. The MIRV mod (Gun Nut 4, Science! 4) fires six at once: more damage, much less range.
Tips: A long-range shot whistles loudly, which is your cue to take cover. The MIRV mod may detonate at your feet, mostly when you aim lower than where you stand.

sections.name: Mini nukes
sections.card:
Summary: A small tactical nuclear warhead, about the size of a football, built for nuclear catapult weapons.
Uses: The Fat Man uses them as ammunition. The Nuka-World add-on's Nuka-nuke launcher fires a variant, the Nuka-nuke.
Tips: A weapon emporium set up in a settlement sells them. Super mutant suiciders carry some; kill one before it detonates, sparing its right arm, to loot its nuke.

sections.name: Junk Jet
sections.card:
Summary: A heavy weapon that fires loaded junk, such as tin cans, teddy bears or desk fans.
Uses: Charge a shot for about 1 second for more damage, but shots drop sharply beyond pistol range. Spent junk can be picked up again, but roughly one in ten is lost on contact.
Tips: Find it in the ArcJet Systems building's rocket control room, which opens after you start Call to Arms. Loaded junk still adds to Carry Weight; steel works well, and weightless pre-War money is another choice.

sections.name: Nuka-Cola Quantum
sections.card:
Summary: A soft drink in a clear bottle of glowing blue liquid; strontium-90 makes it glow.
Uses: It heals 40 hit points a second for 10 seconds, plus 100 action points, but adds 5 radiation. It is not addictive, and Survival mode treats it as caffeinated.
Tips: Nuka-Cola and sticker-marked Vault-Tec lunchboxes can drop one, and raider gang tribute chests can hold one. Bottles respawn after pickup.
